title: Submit a volunteer application to Stockton Street Dogs
instructions: Submit an application to learn how Crossover can participate firsthand.

title: Ask Stockton Animal Services about Doggie Day Out
instructions: Ask about sign-up, requirements, paperwork, and orientation.

title: Visit Stockton Animal Services and submit a volunteer application
instructions: Visit the shelter, deliver the application, and learn about the public visitor experience.

title: Request Animal Services field-call records
instructions: Request field-call records for roaming, stray, abandoned, aggressive, and distressed dogs.

title: Follow up on Animal Services field-call records
instructions: Check for a response to the October 20 request. Review the data only after it is received; document missing fields and limitations.

title: Review source context for the first field visit
instructions: Review the published Louis Park and Stanislaus Street accounts and recent unverified sightings before choosing safe public observation areas. Treat the reports as historical leads, not current conditions.

title: Visit St. Mary's and learn how people care for dogs.
instructions: Visit St. Mary's Community Services to learn from people already caring for dogs. Ask how food, veterinary care, volunteers, and referrals are coordinated, what information would improve Crossover's investigation map, where help encounters obstacles, and what other places or people we should investigate. Record actual observations separately from what people tell us. Do not assume dogs are strays or abandoned; document only what is learned during the visit.

title: Verify reported conditions in South Stockton / District 5
instructions: Investigate the September 24, 2026 KCRA account in which Stockton Street Dogs described increased stray- and dumped-dog encounters, particularly in District 5. First identify a specific current public location through the organization's firsthand knowledge, relevant reports, or Animal Services records. Then conduct a safe field observation and document what is actually present, including zero dogs if none are seen. Distinguish reported claims from firsthand findings and record follow-up questions.

title: Follow up with Stockton Street Dogs
instructions: Check whether the October 7 volunteer application received a response. Ask for the current status and evidence of progress on Canine Campus, and identify practical approved volunteer or care opportunities, requirements, schedules, and contacts. Record any reply only when received.
checklist: What is the current status of Canine Campus?
What are the next milestones and obstacles?
What other major developments are underway?
What help is most needed right now?
Are there specific approved tasks with a location, schedule, supplies, and participation requirements?
If five new volunteers were available tomorrow, what could they actually do?
What coordination problems prevent willing people from helping?
Do you coordinate feeding or water, and can residents join an established route?
What supplies are useful, where should they be delivered, and who handles veterinary referrals?

title: Follow up with Stockton Animal Services on volunteering
instructions: Check the status of the October 14 volunteer application and the October 12 Doggie Day Out inquiry. Confirm onboarding, orientation, eligibility, scheduling, and practical transport requirements; document a response only if received.

title: Investigate the temporary found-animal foster pathway
instructions: Ask Animal Services who is eligible, how a resident enrolls, who authorizes care and provides supplies or veterinary services, how many places are available, and how intake, reunification, adoption, or other successful outcomes can be verified. Do not treat the publicly described pathway as tested.

title: Monitor the proposed animal-control ordinance
instructions: Check the City Council agenda and legislative record for consideration, amended text, vote, and effective date. Keep the October 19 committee referral separate from any later Council adoption.

title: Contact CBS reporter Charlie Lapastora
instructions: Follow up on the April 6 and June 8 CBS Sacramento reports about abandoned dogs in Stockton. Ask what evidence was gathered, what has happened since, and whether the reporter can connect Crossover with firsthand observers with their permission. Record contact or answers only if they actually occur.
checklist: Isabel Guzman was reportedly documenting abandoned dogs near Stanislaus Street for over a year. What was she documenting, and could you introduce us with her permission?
Did your reporting identify specific areas where dogs were regularly found, beyond the general locations mentioned in the articles?
What happened to the dogs featured in your April report? Were they rescued, reunited, or otherwise helped?
How were the estimates of 200–400 street dogs established? Is there underlying documentation?
Have you learned anything new about the situation, the rescue efforts, or the proposed Safe Grounds project since your reports?
